research.job_description_summary: Cognizant's official GenC page describes Generation Cognizant as its hiring and development programme for entry-level talent in India, with campus and off-campus drives, assessments that test communication, aptitude and/or technical skills depending on the role, interviews, and no service bond. The page names no job titles, tracks or eligibility criteria. Secondary sources describe GenC, GenC Next and GenC Elevate tracks assigned by assessment score.
limitations: The official GenC page lists the process in general terms only; it names no roles, tracks, eligibility, assessment patterns or cutoffs. The GenC Next and GenC Elevate track names and pay bands come from secondary sources (JobRise 2026-02-11, unsourced cutoffs).

The only candidate-attributed material found is two short accounts in a 2023 article (updated 2024) on placementpreparation.io, which are generic about rounds and name no specific questions beyond SQL basics and joins; those items are marked low confidence.
The JobRise guide says it spoke with 30+ candidates but does not attribute its lists of most-asked questions to individuals, so those lists were used only as topic context (class D).
A second placementpreparation.io page is partly behind a login wall; its visible sample problems are editorial and not candidate-attributed.
That page's meta description mentions another company, suggesting a copy error; its cluster descriptions (Java/SQL/web and SQL/Python/cloud) are unconfirmed.
Aptitude, communication and debugging items are original practice items.
Because the track names are secondary-sourced, track-specific question allocation is a proposed structure, not documented.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.

questions.subtopic: GROUP BY, HAVING and window functions
questions.prompt: Write a query to show departments with an average salary above 60,000, and explain how a window function like RANK differs from GROUP BY.
questions.relevance_to_role: ANSI SQL is part of both Elevate technical clusters per a secondary source.
questions.expected_answer: SELECT dept_id, AVG(salary) FROM Employee GROUP BY dept_id HAVING AVG(salary) > 60000; GROUP BY collapses rows into groups, while window functions like RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) compute per-row values without collapsing.
follow_ups: How do you get the top earner per department?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/cognizant-genc/interview-experience/.

questions.prompt: What is a closure in JavaScript? Give an example and one practical use.
questions.relevance_to_role: JavaScript is part of Elevate cluster 1 per a secondary source.
questions.expected_answer: A closure is a function that remembers variables from its defining scope even after that scope has finished. Example: a counter factory returning an increment function. Uses: data privacy, callbacks, memoization.
follow_ups: What goes wrong with var in a loop callback?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/cognizant-genc/interview-experience/.

questions.prompt: Explain the CSS box model and the difference between content-box and border-box.
questions.relevance_to_role: HTML and CSS are part of Elevate cluster 1 per a secondary source.
questions.expected_answer: Each element is content plus padding, border and margin. With content-box, width excludes padding and border; with border-box, width includes them, which makes layout sizing easier.
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/cognizant-genc/interview-experience/.

questions.prompt: What are cloud regions and availability zones, and why do they matter for reliability?
questions.relevance_to_role: Cloud fundamentals are part of Elevate cluster 2 per a secondary source.
questions.expected_answer: A region is a geographic area with several isolated availability zones (data-centre groups). Deploying across zones survives a single-zone failure; regions help latency and data-residency rules.
follow_ups: How would you design for region failure?
common_mistakes: Calling a zone a single server
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/cognizant-genc/interview-experience/.

questions.prompt: What is a generator in Python and what is a decorator? Give a use for each.
questions.relevance_to_role: Python is part of Elevate cluster 2 per a secondary source.
questions.expected_answer: A generator yields values lazily, saving memory for large sequences. A decorator wraps a function to add behaviour (logging, caching, auth) without changing its code.
follow_ups: Difference between a list and a generator?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/cognizant-genc/interview-experience/.

questions.prompt: Explain GET vs POST and what status codes 200, 201, 404 and 500 mean.
questions.relevance_to_role: Web technologies are part of Elevate cluster 1 per a secondary source.
questions.expected_answer: GET reads data (safe, idempotent, params in the URL); POST sends data to create or process (body, not idempotent). 200 OK, 201 Created, 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error.
follow_ups: Which method is idempotent: PUT or POST?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/cognizant-genc/interview-experience/.

questions.prompt: Explain the SOLID principles with a one-line example for each.
questions.relevance_to_role: SOLID is listed in a 2026 Cognizant guide's technical topics.
questions.expected_answer: S: one reason to change per class. O: open for extension, closed for modification. L: subclasses must be usable as the base type. I: small, specific interfaces. D: depend on abstractions, not concrete classes.
follow_ups: Which one do you apply most?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://jobrise.io/en/blog/cognizant-interview-questions-freshers-2026/.

questions.prompt: What is the Singleton pattern, and how do you implement it thread-safely?
questions.relevance_to_role: Design patterns are listed in a 2026 Cognizant guide's technical topics.
questions.expected_answer: Singleton ensures one instance with a global access point. Make the constructor private; use eager initialisation, double-checked locking with volatile, or a holder class/enum for thread safety.
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://jobrise.io/en/blog/cognizant-interview-questions-freshers-2026/.
